sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Mayank Krishna S Chandel,Ram Niwas Singh,Vinod Kumar Chandel
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sunil Kumar Tiwari
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.

1. Heard Mr. Mayank Krishna S Chandel, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and Mr. Sunil Kumar Tiwari, the learned counsel for first informant/opposite party-2.
2.
Perused the record.

3. Instant bail application has been filed by applicant-Mohd.Adil seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 154 of 2023 under Sections 363, 366 I.P.C. and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Link Road, District- Ghaziabad, during the pendency of trial.

4. Record shows that in respect of an incident, which is alleged to have occurred on 30.04.2023, a delayed F.I.R. dated 01.05.2023 was lodged by first informant Rita Misra (mother of the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No. 154 of 2023 under Sections 363 I.P.C., Police Station- Link Road, District- Ghaziabad.
In the aforesaid F.I.R. a solitary unknown person has been arraigned as an accused.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. The gravamen of the allegations made in the F.I.R is to the effect that the daughter of first informant namely X, who is aged about 14 years had gone out of her home but has not returned.
6. After the aforementioned F.I.R. was registered, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of afore-mentioned case crime number in terms of Chapter XII Cr.P.C.
The prosecutrix was recovered on 10.05.2023.
Thereafter, statement of prosecutrix was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C, copy of which is on record at page 27 of the paper book.
In her aforesaid statement, the prosecutrix has not supported the F.I.R.
To the contrary, she has stated that she herself accompanied the applicant and thereafter physical relations were maintained by applicant with the prosecutrix itself.
Subsequently, prosecutrix was requested for her internal medical examination.
The prosecutrix in her statement before the Doctor, who medically examined her has stated that applicant forcibly dislodged her modesty.
The Doctor, who medically examined the prosecutrix, did not find any signs on the body of prosecutrix so as to denote commission of sexual assault.

However,
with regard to the private part of the prosecutrix, the Doctor opined as under:
"Hymen - Old torn healed."
7.
Ultimately, the statement of prosecutrix was recorded under Sectiion 164 Cr.P.C., which is on record at page 25 of the paper book.

In her aforesaid statement the prosecutrix has departed from her previous statement under section 161 Cr.P.C. and has now stated that deliberately and forcibly twice physical relations were established by applicant with the prosecutrix.
8. Investigating Officer examined first informant and other witnesses under Section 161 Cr.P.C. .
Witnesses so examined have substantially supported the F.I.R.

On the basis of above and other material collected by him during course of investigation, he came to the conclusion that offence under Sections 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 POCSO Act are made out against applicant.

Ultimately,
Investigating Officer submitted the charge-sheet dated 25.06.2023 against applicant whereby the applicant has been charge-sheeted under Sections 363, 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 POCSO Act.
9. Instant application for bail came up for orders on 07.08.2023 and this Court passed the following order:

"Heard Mr. Mayank Krishna S. Chandel, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and Mr. Sunil Kumar Tiwari, the learned counsel for first informant.
Rejoinder affidavit filed by learned counsel for applicant in Court today which is taken on record.
Learned counsel for applicant contends that age of the prosecutrix is sought to be determined on the basis of school level certificate of Class- IV of the prosecutrix.
However, by virtue of the provisions contained in Section 94 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, the same cannot be relied upon for determining the age of the prosecutrix.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
No document in consonance with the above has been collected Mohd.Adil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147275822/
2 by the Investigating Officer.

entities.text: Mohd.Adil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of above, it is hereby provided that Chief Medical Officer, District Ghaziabad shall get the radiological test/ossification test of the prosecutrix conducted.
The requisite report regarding above be submitted before this Court on or before 30.8.2023.
Put up as fresh on 4.9.2023.
Subsequent to above order dated 07.08.2023, the prosecutrix was medically examined for determination of her age.
The Chief Medical Officer concerned accordingly conducted the ossification test of the prosecutrix for determination of her age.
As per said document, the prosecutrix is reported to be aged about more than 13 years.
11. Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is innocent.
He is not named in the F.I.R..
Though applicant is a charge-sheeted accused yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
With reference to the statement of the prosecutrix as recorded under Section 161 he submits that the prosecutrix is a willing and a consenting party.
The prosecutrix has departed from her earlier statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. in her subsequent statement before the Doctor as well as in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
He submits that the contradiction has emerged in her aforesaid statements remains unexplained upto this stage.
Even otherwise no signs were found on the body of the prosecutrix so as to denote the commission of sexual assault.
As such, the prosecutrix is a willing and consenting party.
Applicant is a young boy aged about 19 years and is a student of Class XIth.
Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in custody since 12.05.2023.
As such, he has undergone more than four months of incarceration.

Police report (charge-sheet) in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted, therefore the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallised.
However, upto this stage, no such incriminating circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
On the above premise, he submits that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
12. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. for State and the learned counsel representing first informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
They submit that since the applicant is a charge sheeted accused therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
As per medical opinion, the prosecutrix is a young girl aged about 13 years whose modesty was dislodged by applicant.
It is thus contended that no sympathy be shown by this Court in favour of applicant.
Prosecutrix is a young girl of tender age.
Even if there was consent given by the prosecutrix, the same is immaterial.
To buttress their submissions they have relied upon the judgement of Supreme court in X (Minor) Vs. The State of Jharkhand and Another ( 2022 Live Law (SC) 194.

entities.text: X (Minor) Vs. The State of Jharkhand and Another ( 2022 Live Law (SC) 194
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On the Mohd.Adil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147275822/
3 aforesaid premise, it is thus urged that no good ground exits to enlarge the applicant on bail.

entities.text: Mohd.Adil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, present applicant for bail is liable to be rejected.
13. When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.

14. Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, the learned counsel for first informant, upon consideration of material on record, evidence, gravity and nature of offence, accusations made as well as complicity of applicant coupled with the fact that as per medical opinion age of the prosecutrix is said to be more than 13 years, therefore, by virtue of law laid down by Apex Court in X (Minor) (supra), even if there is consent of the prosecutrix, the same is immaterial, therefore irrespective of the submission urged by learned counsel for applicant in support of this application for bail, this Court does not find any sufficient or good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
15.
As a result, present application for bail thus fails and is liable to be rejected.
16. It is accordingly rejected.
